clue.text: See 18
No end to the contention in this old Balkan state

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the following word is cut off

parts.note: the short word with its last letter removed
a race is a contest, a contention between rivals

explanation.surface: A historian notes that some ancient Balkan land was forever embroiled in quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: THRACE is the old region north of the Aegean, now split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient kingdom and later Roman province in the south-east of the Balkan peninsula.

clue.text: Preserve the business graduate in wood

indicators.note: the graduate is placed inside the timber, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a tree, and its timber
Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a business-school graduate safe inside a wooden box.
explanation.walkthrough: The wooden box suggests a coffin, which suits the funereal answer; MBA is the standard degree abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it chemically so it is preserved against decay.

clue.text: Right police car crashes into convertible

parts.note: standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: a car that crashes is smashed out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A news snippet: a squad car on the right smashes into an open-topped car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' looks like the car; it is the mathematical sense, as reciprocal relations can be turned round and still hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are reciprocal can be interchanged or swapped for one another, which is what convertible means in logic and maths.

clue.text: Harpagon's promise remains herein

indicators.note: herein says the word sits inside the clue's own text, spanning the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Something Harpagon once pledged survives in this document.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpagon is the money-grubbing title character of Molière's comedy L'Avare (The Miser); his name has become a byword for avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpagon is the archetypal stingy hoarder of French drama, the miser of Molière's play.

clue.text: "Some are born to _____ night" (Blak)

parts.note: a gap-fill: supply the missing word from the famous line
the poet's name lacks its final letter, a hint at the missing word itself

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from William Blake's Auguries of Innocence: 'Some are born to sweet delight, / Some are born to endless night.' Blake printed without his last letter is Blake with the end gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing adjective describes a night that never finishes, one with no conclusion at all.

clue.text: Ornaments M-Matabele used

indicators.note: used letters are worked over and reshaped, so they come out in another order

parts.note: the stammered name supplies the letters, the extra M included

explanation.surface: A stammering description of decorations once worn by the Matabele people of southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is there only to supply a second M.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblemata is the plural of emblema, an inlaid decoration or raised ornament on a vessel or floor.

clue.text: Clean the French dish out

parts.note: as in 'do the kitchen', meaning clean it
a French definite article

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: wash up the French serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like a plate to wash, but 'dish out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out is to hand out or distribute in portions, exactly as one dishes out food or advice.

clue.text: Looks at Hell, sunless with this

definitions.text: Looks at Hell, sunless with this

indicators.note: without sun means the abbreviation for sun, a single letter, is dropped

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
the underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Someone gazes into the inferno, shielded from its glare by something.
explanation.walkthrough: S for sun is a standard abbreviation; HADES loses it. The whole clue also describes the answer: wearing one, you look out shaded from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn on the forehead to keep glare off the eyes, leaving the wearer shaded.

clue.text: They are said to be happy Ovaltinies without her

definitions.text: They are said to be happy

indicators.note: without means leaving something out, so one word is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: the club song ran 'We are the Ovaltineys, little girls and boys'
a female, one of the girls

explanation.surface: A wistful aside that the radio club children are only cheerful when no woman is around.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ovaltineys were a 1930s children's radio club sponsored by the Ovaltine malt drink. Remove GIRL from GIRLS AND BOYS and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase 'happy as a sandboy' makes these the people idiomatically famed for contentment.

clue.text: Mrs de Winter's about to leave, which sounds vile!

definitions.note: a rebec is an instrument, sounding like 'viol'

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so those letters are removed from the name

parts.note: the first wife in Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca
circa, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Mrs de Winter is about to depart, and someone finds the whole affair disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vile' is a homophone joke: a rebec is a member of the viol family of stringed instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed stringed instrument, an ancestor of the fiddle and kin to the viol.

clue.text: Officer ordering vessel to change course

parts.note: a submarine
to alter something is to change it
north, a compass heading or course

explanation.surface: A commander instructs a ship to turn onto a new heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whole order; in fact the vessel, the change and the heading are three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain, such as a lieutenant.

clue.text: Let's do it his way with notes

definitions.text: Let's do it his way with notes

parts.note: the surface reads as a suggestion to follow someone's method
really, 'Let's Do It' is a song title, and its writer did it in music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's Do It, Let's Fall in Love' is a 1928 song by the American songwriter famed for witty lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: The American composer and lyricist wrote 'Let's Do It' and set its words to his own melody.

clue.text: Fish from the c-centre

parts.note: the stammered initial letter
the hub is the centre of a wheel or activity

explanation.surface: Someone stammers that a fish comes from the middle of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer gives a lone C to go before the synonym for centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, common in European rivers.

clue.text: Mr Rusbridger's joint superintendency

parts.note: Alan Rusbridger was the Guardian's editor, so 'Mr Rusbridger's' is the editor's
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A reference to the Guardian editor's bad hip, or to the paper's shared management.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Rusbridger edited the Guardian, which published this puzzle, from 1995 to 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorship is the post of being in charge of a publication, a role of supervision and control.

clue.text: Sharia justice thus applied anyhow?

parts.note: read literally, a punishment that removes a thief's limb
the plain meaning: casually, without care

explanation.surface: A grim question about how religious law punishes theft.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as off-handed-ly, the word describes a sentence of amputation; whole, it means carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something offhandedly or anyhow means doing it casually and without much care or thought.

clue.text: The handwriting, I hear you let slip, could be tubular

parts.note: fist is an informal word for a person's handwriting

indicators.note: what I hear is how the phrase is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: to let something slip is to lose it

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a careless remark about handwriting might reveal something.
explanation.walkthrough: Fist meaning handwriting is old slang ('he writes a good fist').
explanation.definitionFit: Fistulose describes something formed like a pipe or hollow reed, hollow and cylindrical.

clue.text: Exchanging this, some spell "emphasize", stopping at nothing with "emphasise"!

definitions.note: a verb defining a musical direction meaning emphasised

parts.note: spellers who write emphasise put S for Z
'at' as written plus O for nothing
the remaining letters follow on

explanation.surface: A wry note on the s/z spelling war between British and American English.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as the phrase 'S for Z at O'. Sforzato is an Italian musical direction for a sudden strong accent on a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Sforzato marks a note to be played with sudden forceful accent, so it tells the player to stress it.

clue.text: What Sir Stanley Matthews did with the olive oil?

parts.note: the famous footballer's skill of running with the ball at his feet
a cook letting oil fall in small drops over a dish

explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Matthews was an English footballer of the 1930s to 1960s, renowned as a winger who ran past defenders with the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer runs with the ball in short touches, and a cook lets oil fall in drops; one verb covers both.

clue.text: Maths maestro felt … er … uncomfortable with this hypothesis

indicators.note: uncomfortable suggests squirming and shifting, so the letters are restless and rearranged

parts.note: every letter of these words, the hesitation included

explanation.surface: A mathematician hesitates, squirming over a famously hard conjecture.
explanation.walkthrough: The '... er' is the stammer of discomfort, and it supplies the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre de Fermat's conjecture about whole-number powers stayed unproved for over three centuries until Andrew Wiles in 1994.

clue.text: 3 friend of Dickens
In a whip-round, time is complete

parts.note: as written

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face backwards, so the whip is read from its end

parts.note: a cat, short for cat o' nine tails, is a whip
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Collecting money from colleagues for a gift takes time but leaves everything whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like the office collection; split, it is a cat (whip) turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means whole and undamaged, with nothing missing, so the thing is complete.

clue.text: Wax cheaper than Job's wisdom?

definitions.meaning: first name of the American-born British comedian whose surname is Wax
Job 28:18 says the price of wisdom is above rubies

explanation.walkthrough: Ruby Wax is a comedian and TV presenter well known in Britain. The Book of Job says wisdom is worth more than rubies, so the gem is cheaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is both the comedian's first name and the red gemstone the Bible ranks below wisdom in value.

clue.text: See 24
He''s gone into spasm! He's drunk too much tea!

definitions.note: a clause defining a noun: one who has done this

indicators.note: something gone into another thing is now inside it

parts.note: a tic is a muscular spasm
the pronoun as written

explanation.surface: A man twitches violently from overdoing the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Too much caffeine brings on twitching, so the spasm fits the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A theic is a person who drinks excessive amounts of tea, suffering from overindulgence in it.

clue.text: Miss the point of a 10's love song

definitions.text: Miss the point of a 10's love song

parts.note: the surface reads as failing to understand something
really, the young lady who is the whole point of a poem about an army officer in love

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the answer to 10 across. John Betjeman's poem 'A Subaltern's Love Song' adores 'Miss J. Hunter Dunn', a sporty girl from Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the young woman, addressed as Miss, whom the subaltern in Betjeman's poem loves and celebrates.

clue.text: Part 1 of 3 and 19 declaration from Dumas

definitions.text: Part 1 of 3 and 19 declaration from Dumas

parts.note: the first half of a pledge that is both reciprocal and mutual
the motto of the Three Musketeers

explanation.walkthrough: 3 and 19 are cross-references to the answers reciprocal and mutual. The musketeers' motto in Dumas's novel is 'All for one, one for all', a reciprocal pledge; this is its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase opens the Three Musketeers' motto, a promise of loyalty running in both directions between them.

clue.text: African utterance hard on a major powers

parts.note: standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
as written
the United States, a superpower

explanation.surface: A statement from Africa that comes down hard on the great powers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hausa is a language spoken widely in Nigeria and Niger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausa is a major language of West Africa, so it is a form of African speech.

clue.text: De Niro, 'e might become an Establishment figure

indicators.note: might become says the letters could turn into something else when reorganised

parts.note: the actor's name with the dropped-aitch 'e supplying an E

explanation.surface: A Cockney muses that Robert De Niro might yet become a pillar of the British establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Establishment with a capital E hints at the established Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinee is someone being ordained into the clergy, a figure of the Established Church.

clue.text: Verona's family court going out with a whimper

indicators.note: going out round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation for court
'a' as written plus pule, to whimper

explanation.surface: A Veronese household's case at court ends feebly rather than with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out with a whimper' echoes Eliot's 'not with a bang but a whimper', but here going out means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capulets are Juliet's family, one of the two feuding houses of Verona in Shakespeare's play.
